_comment: The two INIT replies that Loop #92's extension rule has to hold for.
The gate compares our SFTP server with the real `sftp-server.exe` on
the machine it runs on.  The INIT reply's EXTENSION LIST is not the
protocol's -- it is the server's, and it changes with the server's
version.  Measured, with the real tool, on two machines:
this_machine  -- OpenSSH 7.9p1 (Win32-OpenSSH), the build on the
machine these gates were developed on.  179 bytes.
the_runner  -- the inbox Windows OpenSSH, which a GitHub runner
has.  250 bytes.  It moved `statvfs@openssh.com` from "1" to
"2", added `fstatvfs@openssh.com`, and dropped the four
extensions (`limits`, `expand-path`, `copy-data`,
`home-directory`) that the older one had.
So a gate that compares the INIT reply BYTE FOR BYTE is measuring
whether this machine's OpenSSH is the same version as the runner's.
That is the same defect Loop #69 found in `host/sshd_setup.mjs`: a
claim about the machine that is not in the repository.
The rule the gate uses instead is in `host/verify_loop92.mjs`, and
`host/verify_loop92_init_rule.mjs` exercises it against these bytes
and against three negative controls.  The bytes are kept HERE, in
the repository, so the rule is checked against both machines'
OpenSSH on every run -- and so the next version of the real server
can be ADDED to the list rather than rediscovered.
This file is written by `.loop93/build_init_replies.mjs` from the
measured bytes.  Hand-typed hex is how the first version of it came
to differ from the measurement by six bytes.
